learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge of classical probability theory, axiomatic probability, random variables and vectors, analytical methods, limit laws.
An overview of random processes theory.
Ability to construct simple probabilistic models.
Ability to perform relevant probabilistic calculations.
Demonstrate acquisition of basic knowledge of probability theory, discrete and continuous random variables, and the fundamentals of random processes.
Demonstrate ability to apply acquired theory to identify appropriate probabilistic models for random phenomena.
Demonstrate ability to solve probability calculation problems.

syllabus_topics: Probability: Probability spaces and their properties
Elements of combinatorial calculus and classical probability problems
Random Variables (RV): Definition of discrete RV
Discrete density and distribution function: definition and properties
Notable discrete RVs: Bernoulli, binomial, geometric, Poisson
Classification of RVs: absolutely continuous, discrete, and mixed
Notable absolutely continuous RVs: uniform, exponential, Gaussian
Expected value, variance, moments: definition and properties
Moment generating function and characteristic function
Joint probability density and its properties
Expected value of RVe and moments of RVe
Sequences of Random Variables: Sequences of RVs
Convergence in distribution, in probability, in mean
Law of large numbers and central limit theorem
Spectral analysis in filtering random processes
teaching_methods: Use of teaching technologies (Moodle and/or other teaching tools, software, videos, quizzes, Wooclap)
Homework exercises with subsequent solution illustration

assessment_methods.method: Written exam consisting of problem solving

assessment_rules: The written exam consists of solving problems to verify mastery of theory and calculation techniques. Students must demonstrate acquisition of basic knowledge of probability theory, discrete and continuous random variables, and the fundamentals of random processes. They must also demonstrate the ability to apply the acquired theory to identify appropriate probabilistic models for random phenomena and to solve probability calculation problems.
institution: Università degli Studi di Padova — Information Engineering (L-8)
degree: Laurea in Information Engineering (Information Engineering), classe L-8 R Ingegneria dell'informazione
